state_legislation_2026.session: Colorado General Assembly, 2026 regular session; adjourned sine die 2026-05-13
state_legislation_2026.headline: Pueblo City Council formally opposed three surveillance/privacy bills on 2026-02-09. ALL THREE DIED. Colorado ended the 2026 session with no statute regulating ALPRs, no statute regulating law-enforcement surveillance technology generally, and no ban on government purchase of third-party personal data. Every constraint on Pueblo's RTCC/Flock/ShotSpotter/drone stack is therefore local and discretionary.

bills_opposed_by_pueblo.title: Ban Government Access Historical Location Information Database ('PEEPS Act' - Protecting Everyone from Excessive Police Surveillance)
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.final_action: Pulled by its own sponsors at Senate Second Reading on 2026-04-29; recorded as 'Senate Second Reading Laid Over to 07/04/2026 - No Amendments,' a parking maneuver past sine die. Died without a floor vote.
history: 2026-01-28 Introduced in Senate, assigned to Judiciary
2026-02-23 Senate Judiciary PASSED with amendments L.001, L.003, L.005, L.007, L.008, L.009, L.010; referred to Appropriations
2026-04-21 Senate Appropriations PASSED with amendment L.013; referred to Committee of the Whole
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.sponsors: Sens. Judy Amabile (D-Boulder) and Lynda Zamora Wilson (R-Colorado Springs); Reps. Yara Zokaie (D-Fort Collins) and Kenny Nguyen (D-Broomfield). Bipartisan.
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.why_it_died: Amabile: 'We didn't have the votes.' She also said she was told Gov. Polis would veto it; the Governor's office confirmed SB26-070 'went much further' than codifying best practices and 'would have negatively impacted public safety.' Amabile quoted colleagues saying 'I just can't vote for this because I'm getting hammered by law enforcement.'
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.opposition_coalition: Colorado Association of Chiefs of Police, Colorado District Attorneys' Council, County Sheriffs of Colorado, Colorado State Fire Chiefs, Colorado Municipal League, and 'several city governments' (unenumerated - Pueblo's Feb 9 resolution is one of the city positions in that bucket). Named municipal witness: Colorado Springs Police Deputy Chief Jeff Jensen ('a warrant would be almost impossible to obtain').
would_have_required_of_pueblo_pd: Warrant to query historical location data more than 72 hours old (exigency exception preserved; hotlists not banned)
~30-day retention cap absent a legitimate reason
No sharing outside the collecting jurisdiction without a warrant
Logging of when and why each query is made
Public annual report disclosing the number and location of surveillance devices
Attorney General enforcement; suppression of unlawfully obtained evidence
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.next_round: Amabile will 'come back next year and do more work in the interim.' Rep. Nguyen: 'I guarantee you, we're going to be on the same conversation, probably with a new governor, and hopefully we can make out some form of compromise.'

bills_opposed_by_pueblo.title: Use of Surveillance Technology by Law Enforcement ('SAFE Act' - Surveillance Accountability and Freedom Ensured)
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.final_action: Postponed Indefinitely in Senate Judiciary 6-1 on 2026-05-06
history: 2026-01-28 Introduced in Senate, assigned to Judiciary
2026-02-23 Senate Judiciary: Lay Over Unamended; amendment(s) FAILED
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.sponsors: Prime sponsor Sen. Lynda Zamora Wilson (R-Colorado Springs); no co-sponsors listed on the bill page.
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.why_it_died: Colorado Politics attributes its death to governor veto threats. Killed formally in committee one week before sine die.
would_have_required_of_pueblo_pd: Surveillance tech used only for lawful purposes directly related to public safety or an active investigation
Traffic cameras and ALPRs restricted to public spaces for enumerated enforcement purposes
Drone use tied to federal aviation regulations
Mandatory data destruction after retention periods expire
Ban on selling data; inter-agency sharing only for active investigations
Compliance information provided to residents at no cost
Biennial audits by the Attorney General
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.local_significance: Would have touched every layer of Pueblo's stack simultaneously - ShotSpotter, BRINC drones, fixed park cameras, body-worn cameras, Flock ALPRs, Genetec Community Connect. Its death means none of those are subject to any state published-use-policy or audit mandate. Facial recognition in Colorado remains warrantless as a matter of state law.

bills_opposed_by_pueblo.title: Ban Government Purchase of Personal Data from Third Party
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.city_of_pueblo_position: Opposed (resolution adopted 2026-02-09); the city's resolution called the bill 'harmful to public safety'
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.final_action: Postponed Indefinitely in House Judiciary 6-5 on 2026-04-22
history: 2026-01-14 Introduced in House, assigned to Judiciary
2026-02-25 House Judiciary witness testimony and discussion
2026-04-22 Motion to refer to Appropriations FAILED 5-6
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.sponsors: Reps. Jennifer Bacon (D) and Ken DeGraaf (R); Sen. Lisa Cutter (D). Cross-ideological progressive-plus-libertarian coalition.
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.would_have_required: Prohibited government entities and law enforcement from purchasing or otherwise obtaining for anything of value specified personal data from third parties, and restricted agency-to-agency sharing of it. Exceptions: judicial warrant, subpoena, court order, individual consent, life-safety emergency. Included a private cause of action and exclusion of improperly obtained data from court proceedings.
bills_opposed_by_pueblo.local_significance: CLOSEST of the three - died by one vote, twice, on the same day. A single flipped House Judiciary member sends it to Appropriations. Highest-leverage 2027 target. Pueblo took its sharpest rhetorical position on the bill that came nearest to passing. Received essentially no statewide press (Colorado Politics' roundup omits it entirely).

bills_that_PASSED_and_bind_local_agencie.status: BECAME LAW - signed by Gov. Polis 2026-05-27
bills_that_PASSED_and_bind_local_agencie.sponsors: Reps. Katie Stewart and Javier Mabrey; Sens. Judy Amabile and Mike Weissman

Sheriff must coordinate with the BWC vendor to implement a strip-search tag and apply 'the most restrictive level of access available' to that footage

bills_that_PASSED_and_bind_local_agencie.pueblo_impact: Applies directly to PCSO's new 672-bed detention center. Creates a new, dated, CORA-requestable document trail.

bills_that_PASSED_and_bind_local_agencie.status: BECAME LAW - cleared legislature 2026-05-11, signed by Gov. Polis 2026-06-04

county_detention_2026.event: New Pueblo County detention center opened early May 2026; all inmates transferred by 2026-07-11
county_detention_2026.location: 3830 Medal of Honor Blvd, Pueblo west side
county_detention_2026.beds: 672 (reported as 627 by one outlet - use 672 with the discrepancy noted); ~150 more than the 1980-built downtown jail

county_detention_2026.features: Marketed as the first net-zero-energy jail in the US, with on-site solar array; medical clinics, kitchen, treatment areas

county_detention_2026.driver: Chronic overcrowding - populations exceeding design capacity by upwards of 200 at times - plus state authorities threatening sanctions over non-compliance.
county_detention_2026.sheriff_quote: Lucero at the opening: 'We do have the ability out here if we come close to capacity at 680, that we can then expand on this 33 acres to bring another cell block in.'

NO SOURCE states Pueblo County holds or seeks any ICE/USMS contract - this is a risk to monitor, NOT a finding. Note that Colorado law bars local governments from contracting with PRIVATE civil immigration detention facilities; a county-run facility is a different legal question.
county_detention_2026.new_statutory_hooks: HB26-1123 (effective 2026-05-27) applies - BWC recording of strip searches, restricted-access tagging, annual report to the jail standards advisory committee and the Attorney General. HB26-1276 (effective 2026-08-12) mandates unannounced state inspections at least four times yearly of immigration detention facilities.

flock_alpr_expansion.status: Pueblo PD acquiring 12 Flock ALPR cameras, with 4 already operational
flock_alpr_expansion.reported: 2026-05 (approximate - the KOAA article carries no visible publication date; search index places it May 2026)
flock_alpr_expansion.other_inventory_disclosed: Cloud-runner cameras; four mobile camera trailers for redeployment to 'high-crime areas'; ShotSpotter; drone-as-first-responder; fixed park cameras at Mitchell Park, Mineral Palace Park, City Park, and El Centro/El Central Park.
flock_alpr_expansion.department_claim: Deputy Chief Jim Martin: the systems 'aren't used for random surveillance,' and officers 'must have specific reasons to search license plates, and those reasons must be documented in the system.' This is a public claim that an internal audit log EXISTS - and with SB26-070 dead there is no state audit or public-reporting requirement behind it. CORA-requestable and the natural test of the department's own stated policy.
flock_alpr_expansion.not_disclosed: Dollar amount, funding source, contract term, and whether council ever approved it. A 12-camera buy may sit below the procurement threshold forcing a public council vote - which is itself the finding.
flock_alpr_expansion.statewide_contrast: Denver added contract terms imposing a $100,000 fine and possible termination for sharing ALPR data with the federal government for immigration enforcement, barred federal task-force officers from access, and had Flock disable Denver's data in the nationwide lookup (CBS Colorado, 2025-10-22). Denver Auditor Tim O'Brien REFUSED to sign the city's Flock contract on 2026-02-19 after the mayor bypassed council: 'I just want that data secure, so that you and I as citizens don't have our data being exposed to people that shouldn't have it.' Pueblo has no publicly known equivalent safeguard.
flock_alpr_expansion.gaps: Whether Pueblo PD participates in Flock's national lookup network and whether its data has been queried for immigration purposes - Pueblo does not appear in any reachable Flock transparency-portal index and no Pueblo-specific audit was found. Whether the 4 camera trailers are Flock or a separate vendor.

priority_followups_2026_07_29: HIGHEST PRIORITY: get Sheriff-elect Allen Medina on the record before January 2027 on (a) whether he adopts, rewrites, or drops the 2025-01-23 ICE non-cooperation pledge; (b) whether PCSO will rent beds in the new 672-bed facility to ICE/USMS; (c) PCSO's ALPR and RTCC data-sharing posture. He is running on 'transparent about everything that we do,' which makes public questions hard to deflect.
Update EVERY citation of Sheriff Lucero's Jan 2025 ICE pledge across data/ and reports/ with 'policy of an outgoing sheriff; term ends Jan 2027.'

Because there is now NO state ALPR statute, reframe the local ask from 'support the state bill' to 'adopt a local surveillance-use ordinance' (published use policies, retention limits, query audit logs, annual public reporting, no federal immigration sharing - i.e. the SB26-070/071 provisions enacted municipally). Denver's contract terms are the nearest Colorado template.

Pull the 2026-02-09 and 2026-02-23 minutes plus the January 2026 organizational meeting minutes from pueblo.us AgendaCenter - roll calls and committee assignments are the biggest gaps in this dataset.
Request Senate Judiciary 2026-02-23, Senate Appropriations 2026-04-21, and House Judiciary 2026-02-25 witness lists from Legislative Council to settle whether any Pueblo official testified.

CORA Pueblo PD for the Flock contract/quote, the ALPR use policy, and the ALPR query audit log with stated reasons (Deputy Chief Martin has publicly asserted this log exists). Ask explicitly whether Pueblo PD shares into Flock's national network and whether any federal immigration agency has queried Pueblo data.

CORA Pueblo County/PCSO for any intergovernmental agreement or bed-rental contract with ICE, USMS, or another federal agency, plus average daily population against the 672 design capacity, and the surveillance system installed in the new facility.
Document the FBI Southern Colorado Safe Streets Task Force relationship - MOU, participating PPD/PCSO personnel, and what data flows through it. New thread.

Draft a neutral surveillance/privacy questionnaire for the Commissioner D3 candidates and the sheriff-elect. Per AGENTS.md, publish questions and any answers as information - do not campaign or target persuasion.
Determine the City of Pueblo procurement threshold requiring a council vote and check the 12-camera Flock buy against it.
Add the November 2026 Governor's race to the watchlist as an upstream determinant of 2027 surveillance legislation.
